_comment: A few lines for each web framework, given to the AI coding tool after the coding rules when the app's package lists name the framework (ADR-143, backlog 0663). Every line is written in this project's own words and names the code rules (data/ast-rules.json) that find the fault it guards against; a line carries those rules' requirements as its citations, so nothing here cites on its own. Each line has at least one `faults` entry: a few lines of that framework's code with the fault, which the named rule must report (crates/sv-check/tests/stack_guidance.rs); they are for the test alone and are never shown. The choice of topics was inspired by Wiz's secure rules files (https://github.com/wiz-sec-public/secure-rules-files, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); none of their text is here. Worth nothing as evidence: no requirement changes status because a line was given.
credit: These lines are StackVet's own. The choice of topics was inspired by Wiz's [secure rules files](https://github.com/wiz-sec-public/secure-rules-files); none of their text is used.

lines.line: Let Jinja escape every value: put HTML in template files and pass values to `render_template`. Never use `|safe`, `Markup(...)`, or `render_template_string` on anything that came from a request.
Serve a stored file with `send_from_directory` and a folder of your own; never pass a name from the request to `open` or `send_file`.
Never switch off CSRF protection (`WTF_CSRF_ENABLED = False`). Flask has none of its own: add Flask-WTF's `CSRFProtect` for every form that changes something (`sv` does not check that it was added).

faults.code: WTF_CSRF_ENABLED = False

lines.line: Never switch on debug mode in the code (`app.run(debug=True)`): its error page lets anyone who reaches it run code on the server.

faults.code:
from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)
app.run(debug=True)

lines.line: Let templates escape every value; never use `mark_safe`, `|safe`, or `{% autoescape off %}` on anything a user wrote.
Query through the ORM. Where raw SQL is needed (`raw`, `extra`, `cursor.execute`), pass values as parameters, never in an f-string or `%`.

faults.code:
from django.db import connection
def find(request):
    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM notes WHERE owner = '{request.GET['who']}'")

lines.line: Never mark a view `@csrf_exempt` that a signed-in person's browser can reach, and keep `CsrfViewMiddleware` in `MIDDLEWARE` (`sv` does not check that it is still there).
Set `DEBUG = False` in the settings the app runs with; read it from the environment if development needs it on.

faults.code: DEBUG = True

lines.line: Before redirecting to a `next` address from the request, check it with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`.
Never build a `FileResponse` path from a request value; look the file up by an id the app chose.
Pass values to SQL as parameters (SQLAlchemy's `text()` with bound values, or the ORM), never in an f-string.
Never call `cors({ origin: true, credentials: true })` or reflect the request's `Origin` with credentials; list the sites that may call the app.

faults.code:
const cors = require('cors');
app.use(cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));

lines.line: Never pass a name from `req.params` or `req.query` to `res.sendFile` or `fs`; look the file up by an id the app chose.
Never `res.redirect` to an address from the request; redirect to a path the app chose.
Serve static files from a folder of their own (`express.static('public')`), never from the folder the server's code is in.
Let React escape values by writing them as `{value}`; never put text from a user or a server into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
Never keep a sign-in token or a password in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`, where any script on the page can read it; let the server set an `HttpOnly` cookie.
Let ERB escape every value; never call `html_safe` or `raw` on anything a user wrote.
Keep forgery protection on; never `skip_forgery_protection` on a controller a signed-in person's browser can reach.

faults.code:
class NotesController < ApplicationController
  skip_forgery_protection
end

lines.line: Give Active Record values as parameters (`where(owner: x)` or `where("owner = ?", x)`), never inside `#{}` in the SQL.

faults.code:
class Note < ApplicationRecord
  def self.for(who)
    find_by_sql("SELECT * FROM notes WHERE owner = '#{who}'")
  end
end

lines.line: Never `redirect_to` an address from `params`; redirect to a path the app chose.

faults.code:
class SessionsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    redirect_to params[:back]
  end
end

lines.line: Never read outside data with `Marshal.load` or `YAML.load`; use JSON, or `YAML.safe_load`.

faults.code:
class ImportController < ApplicationController
  def create
    Marshal.load(request.body.read)
  end
end

lines.line: Render pages with a template engine that escapes (Askama, or Tera with escaping on); never return `Html(format!(...))` with a value in it.
Never let tower-http's `CorsLayer` echo back whatever site calls (`AllowOrigin::mirror_request()`, or `very_permissive()`) together with credentials; list the sites that may call the app.
Let `html/template` escape values; never wrap text from a user in `template.HTML`.
Pass values to `db.Query` and `db.Exec` as `?` or `$1` arguments, never through `fmt.Sprintf`.
